findings.reason: a node taking "re-export" literally places the moved-name import at the top of routing.py and hits ImportError, or to avoid it pulls the 27 retained gc helpers into gc.py — far beyond the declared deliverable and changing the ~44,000-token end state — because the plan asserts the split is behaviour-preserving without naming the inbound edge that makes it work or not.
findings.text: §6 says "routing.py re-exports every moved name, so the twenty-odd production modules that import them from routing keep working unchanged" and "A pure move cannot change behaviour", but the two moved families depend on 29 names that stay in routing.py — the gc family calls GcSweepError, _release_worktree_whole, _live_pointer_worktrees, _stale_run_locks, _git, _release_worktree_whole, _pinnable_unique_commits and 20 more, and the process family calls _write_sender_record and _running_descendants — so gc.py and process_signal.py must each do `from reckon.crew.routing import ...` while routing.py does `from reckon.crew.gc import ...`, a mutual import whose correctness depends entirely on statement order, which the plan never states

findings.reason: the two figures disagree by 526 bytes but the conclusion (over the 50,000 bound, needing this split) is unchanged at either size, so no node's path shifts.
findings.text: §6's "Recounted on 2026-10-14" pairs a byte count with a token count the repository's own estimate does not produce: "208,281 bytes, about 59,660 estimated tokens", but `_tokens_for_bytes` (the ratio the window test imports) gives 59,509 tokens for 208,281 bytes, and 59,660 tokens only for 208,807 bytes, which is what `routing.py` actually measures at HEAD
